summary_html: Agency fails to **disclose required data or reports**, obstructing transparency. Federal statutes require public reporting under CAPTA, FOIA, and Sunshine provisions.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — mandates public availability of child-fatality information  
- **Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552)** — public access to federal records  
- **Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. § 552b)** — open-meeting requirements

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a public body answering a FOIA request must segregate or redact exempt material and disclose the rest, so the City had to produce redacted records even though the requester had not initially asked for redacted material, and it prescribed the Vaughn index and affidavit a body must supply when it withholds.
key_cases.relevance: It defines what a public body must do, and prove, before withholding requested records.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the City was required to provide Mr. Farley this redacted material in response to his original FOIA request

key_cases.case_name: Taylor v. West Virginia Department of Health & Human Resources
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Affirming summary judgment on the retaliatory discharge, Human Rights Act and false light claims of two discharged DHHR lawyers but reversing as to their Whistle-blower Law claims, the Court held that an employer's proffer of an arguably legitimate reason does not entitle it to summary judgment when the motive for the discharge is genuinely disputed.
key_cases.relevance: It is the WV whistle-blower framework protecting agency insiders who report wrongdoing about procurement and program conduct.
key_cases.quote: There is little question that whether petitioners were discharged for retaliatory or discriminatory reasons is replete with disputed issues of material fact which must be resolved by the fact-finder

key_cases.case_name: Daily Gazette Co. v. West Virginia Development Office
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Remanding with directions, the Court held that a public body withholding records under the internal-memoranda exemption must produce a Vaughn index justifying each document and a supporting affidavit, and that the exemption covers only deliberative advice, opinions and recommendations, not ordinary communications with private parties.
key_cases.relevance: It is the foundational WV FOIA rule — that the withholding body bears the burden and may not rely on conclusory or general assertions — which Farley v. Worley later extends to segregation and redaction.
key_cases.quote: The Vaughn index must provide a relatively detailed justification as to why each document is exempt, specifically identifying the reasons why W. Va.Code, 29B-1-4(8) [1977] is relevant
